classification.difficultyReason: Convert bag counts into missing branch probabilities, keep the second bag unchanged across branches, and multiply the two blue probabilities.

content.prompt:
A bag contains three red and four blue marbles, and a second bag contains 5 red and 4 blue.
A marble is selected from each bag.

spec.description: Two-stage tree with R above B at each stage, supplied probabilities 3/7 and 4/9, and terminal events RR, RB, BR, BB. Four missing branch probabilities are answered in adjacent editable dotted clozes identified by their branch associations.
spec.mathematics: First bag: P(R)=3/7, P(B)=4/7. Second bag on either path: P(R)=5/9, P(B)=4/9.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the two source-supplied probabilities appear in the question diagram; missing probabilities are controllable native clozes.

answer.short: 1st bag B: $\frac47$; 2nd bag R after R: $\frac59$; R after B: $\frac59$; B after B: $\frac49$.
answer.worked: The first bag contains 7 marbles, so $P(B)=\frac47$. The second bag contains 9 marbles, so $P(R)=\frac59$ and $P(B)=\frac49$ on both paths. Selecting from the first bag does not change the second bag.
